commemoration.title: Synaxis of the Archangel Michael and the Other Bodiless Powers

_note: Two OCA editions of one hymn. The base is the OCA service-texts DOCX (reference/scrape/2024-11-08.docx, "Prepared by the Department of Liturgical Music and Translations"); the parish sings the OCA engraved-music setting (© 2019 OCA) printed in its choir packet. Register is NOT the whole difference and a ?pronoun=yy render does not reach this wording — see memory project_register_knob_is_service_wide.

_provenance.family_note: OCA. The OCA service-texts DOCX; identical to the stichera row it stands in for.

value.text:
O Michael, the Chief Captain, thou hast been revealed as the brightest attendant of the triply-radiant Godhead. Together with the heavenly powers thou criest out with joy: “Holy art Thou, O Father, Holy art Thou, O Word, also without beginning, Holy art Thou, O Holy Spirit: one glory, one kingdom, one nature,
one Godhead and power!”

value.text:
Michael the Archangel, you have been revealed
as the bright messenger of the tri-luminary Godhead.
Together with the heavenly powers you cry out:
Holy art Thou, O Father
Holy art Thou, O co-eternal Word
Holy art Thou, O Holy Spirit:
One glory, one kingdom, one essence//
one Godhead, one power!
